title: Evaluating the Effect of Activity-Based Method of Teaching Mathematics on Nigerian Secondary School Students’ Achievement in Mathematics
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an activity-based teaching method improves secondary school students’ achievement in mathematics compared with the conventional lecture method. The study is motivated by persistent poor performance in mathematics among Nigerian secondary school students and asks whether a more interactive, student-centered approach can produce better test outcomes.

The intervention was an activity-based mathematics teaching approach applied to topics in circle geometry and construction. The comparison condition was lecture-based instruction. The study used a pretest-posttest quasi-experimental design with intact classes and ANCOVA to adjust for pretest differences, allowing comparison of posttest achievement between the two groups.

Participants were 96 Senior Secondary II students from two government-owned schools in Calabar Metropolis, Cross River State, Nigeria. The paper reports that students in the activity-based group outperformed those in the lecture group on the posttest after controlling for pretest scores. The author concludes that activity-based instruction can increase mathematics achievement and recommends teacher training and the provision of materials to support its use in secondary schools.

identified_tools.name: CAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Computer-assisted instruction or teacher-led instructional intervention used to support learning, typically through structured lessons or activities rather than a specific commercial AI product.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper studied an activity-based teaching method versus lecture method in secondary school mathematics; no AI system, generative model, or named educational technology product was evaluated.

findings.finding_summary: This paper is not an AI-tool study; it reports a quasi-experimental comparison of activity-based teaching versus lecture teaching in mathematics. Students in the activity-based group had higher posttest mean scores (51.71) than the lecture group (29.56) after controlling for pretest scores, with ANCOVA showing a significant group effect (F=114.461, p<0.05, partial eta squared=0.261).

quality_tier_rationale: The paper uses a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with ANCOVA, but it evaluates a conventional teaching method rather than an AI tool. This is empirical education research, but not evidence about generative AI or instructional coaching technology.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported group effect is moderate to large (partial eta squared=0.261), indicating meaningful academic impact for the instructional intervention. However, because the intervention is not an AI tool and the study does not address teacher coaching or feedback systems, the relevance to the requested topic is limited.
